question: What is the main idea behind tele-nursing?

options.A: Replacing all hospital-based nursing staff completely
options.B: Diagnosing rare diseases without doctor approval
options.D: Providing nursing care using telecommunications technology

explanation: You've got this! Tele-nursing simply means using phones, computers, and other tech to deliver professional nursing care when you can't be there in person. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: How does tele-nursing help solve healthcare delivery challenges right here in Nigeria?

options.A: By eliminating the need for clinical nursing education
options.B: By lowering the cost of prescription medications to zero
options.C: By removing the need for any physical hospitals
options.D: By bridging gaps caused by low nurse-to-patient ratios

explanation: Great thinking! Because we often face nurse shortages, using digital tools allows a single nurse to safely reach and support patients spread across wide areas. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h1)

question: Which tool is still the easiest and most widely available for tele-nursing in low-resource settings?

options.B: Dedicated satellite tracking systems for ambulances
options.C: Basic mobile telephony for voice calls and SMS
options.D: High-end virtual reality headsets for surgery

explanation: Spot on! Simple voice calls and text messages require very little internet and work on almost every basic mobile phone our patients carry. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Why do nurses in many Nigerian settings prefer lightweight, low-bandwidth video apps?

options.A: They completely eliminate the need for electricity
options.B: They automatically prescribe drugs without a doctor
options.C: They prevent patients from making phone calls
options.D: They function smoothly on unstable mobile data networks

explanation: Exactly! When mobile data can be unpredictable, using light apps helps keep the conversation going without annoying dropped calls. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h2)

question: Which official body regulates nursing practice and sets standards in Nigeria?

options.A: National Agency for Food and Drug Administration
options.B: Nursing and Midwifery Council of Nigeria
options.C: Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria

explanation: You nailed it! The NMCN is our guiding body responsible for nursing education and practice rules across the country. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: Why is it risky to use normal, unprotected public chat apps to share patient photos?

options.A: It automatically deletes the patient medical history
options.B: It can violate patient confidentiality and data privacy
options.C: It prevents the nurse from writing paper prescriptions
options.D: It charges the hospital high international tax rates

explanation: Safety first! Patient privacy is sacred. Sending sensitive health details over unsecured apps exposes their personal information to breaches. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h3)

question: When you are doing a virtual assessment and can't see the patient clearly, what skill becomes your best friend?

options.C: Physical palpation of deep internal organs
options.D: Active listening and observing tone of voice

explanation: Brilliant! When visual clues are limited, tuning into how the patient sounds helps you pick up on hidden pain, stress, or confusion. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: You are on a video call with a patient experiencing mild breathing trouble. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Diagnose the exact strain of infection through the screen
options.B: Observe breathing patterns and ask the client to describe symptoms clearly
options.C: Send an ambulance immediately without asking any further questions
options.D: Tell the client to turn off the phone and rest quietly

explanation: Well done! Since physical exams are tricky online, watching how they breathe and asking clear questions helps you gather vital clues safely. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h4)

question: Which of these health conditions is best suited for regular tele-nursing check-ins?
explanation: Spot on! Long-term chronic conditions like high blood pressure and diabetes thrive on consistent, routine monitoring rather than one-time emergency care. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: How does tele-nursing actively help reduce hospital readmissions for chronic patients?

options.A: By providing permanent housing inside the main hospital ward
options.B: By catching abnormal vital signs early before complications worsen
options.C: By stopping patients from ever speaking to doctors
options.D: By supplying patients with unlimited free prescription drugs

explanation: Exactly! Catching small warning signs early lets you step in with advice or care before a small issue turns into a major emergency. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a common challenge for tele-nursing in low-resource areas?

options.A: Digital illiteracy among older members of the population
options.B: Erratic electrical power supply causing device shutdowns
options.C: High costs associated with purchasing mobile data bundles
options.D: Excessive availability of free high-speed fiber internet everywhere

explanation: You got it! Free, high-speed fiber internet is definitely not everywhere in resource-limited settings, making it the odd one out. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)

question: How can a nurse manage poor network coverage when trying to reach patients in rural communities?

options.A: By abandoning all forms of digital communication permanently
options.B: By relying entirely on landline telephones built in the 1960s
options.C: By forcing patients to walk twenty kilometers to the nearest city
options.D: By using asynchronous messaging where messages are sent when signal is available

explanation: Smart thinking! Asynchronous messaging (like sending texts that deliver whenever the network flickers back on) is a lifesaver when live signals fail. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T10#GNS113_U1_T10_h6)
